mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum measured by PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 new jobs in a month coincides with stronger consumer confidence and higher S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In periods of high inflation or rising unemployment, PAYEMS > 200000 does not predict positive 20-day SPX returns (Pearson correlation < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (GDPC1) of more than 5% from the prior quarter coincides with a sharp downward revision in 20-day S&P 500 forward expectations, indicating weak demand.
failure_condition: No significant negative relationship between GDPC1 QoQ declines and 20-day forward return revision (beta < -0.3, t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of contracting manufacturing activity (INDPRO < 100) combined with rising consumer prices (CPIAUCSL > 102) create supply-side uncertainty that short-cuts growth expectations and drives S&P 500 60-day forward returns negative.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 100 and CPIAUCSL > 102 in the same month
failure_condition: In non-shock regimes (e.g., steady growth), the combined signal does not predict negative 60-day returns (interaction p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate above 4% for three consecutive months triggers the Federal Reserve to pause rate hikes, which increases the real discount rate and compresses equity valuations, producing negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: When the unemployment rate remains below 4% for 3 months, the trigger does not precede negative 20-day returns (measured by 5-day rolling returns around the trigger).

mechanism_narrative: Sustained strength in housing starts (HOUST > 2000) for two consecutive months reflects growing demand for credit and liquidity, which accelerates corporate investment and drives positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: In periods of high interest rates or supply constraints, HOUST > 2000 does not predict positive 60-day returns (beta < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in consumer inflation expectations (implied by CPIAUCSL under-revision) coincides with a positive surprise in retail sales (PAYEMS), creating a dual signal of deflationary pressure and consumer resilience that boosts 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL revision down > 0.5% AND PAYEMS > 105000 in the same month
failure_condition: In periods of strong inflation, the interaction does not produce significant positive returns (interaction p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index below 105 for three months, despite stable or rising employment (PAYEMS), signals supply-side constraints that reduce business investment and depress 60-day S&P 500 forward expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 105 for 3 consecutive months AND PAYEMS stable (change < 5%)
failure_condition: When employment is expanding strongly (PAYEMS > 110000) during the same period, the signal does not predict negative 60-day returns (interaction p > 0.05).
